title: Options for Enrolling in Medicare with Full Medicaid Benefits
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: If I stay eligible for Medicaid, what are my options for enrolling in Medicare?

accurate_complete: Mentioned can enroll in Original Medicare with Medicaid acting as secondary / supplemental coverage
Mentioned can enroll in a D-SNP (Dual Special Needs Plan)
Explained that Medicaid will help cover Medicare costs (premiums, deductibles, copays)
Mentioned that D-SNPs integrate / coordinate Medicare and Medicaid benefits
accurate_incomplete: Mentioned the D-SNP option but did not explain Medicaid cost-sharing assistance
Mentioned the Original Medicare option but did not mention the D-SNP alternative
Provided some substantive information but missed key details about benefit integration
not_substantive: Counselor did not answer the question
Only said 'you have options' without elaborating
incorrect: Said dual-eligible beneficiaries cannot enroll in Medicare Advantage
Said Medicaid and Medicare cannot work together
Provided materially incorrect information about dual-eligible enrollment options

scoring_notes: All 4 criteria are required for Accurate and Complete. The most commonly missed element is explaining how Medicaid covers Medicare cost-sharing. The 18.9% accurate_complete baseline reflects the complexity of dual-eligible enrollment — most counselors cover part of this but not all components.
